correctness.rationale: At each finite even N, both transformed and arithmetic means of two pooled rank permutations are constant exactly when the second permutation is the complement of the first, because the logit score is strictly increasing and odd under rank complement. Reversal-count expectation has coefficient 2σ/√π per p–q pair; group combinatorics give Λ=∫h²/√π. Fixed-graph factorial moments show that at N²σ→c only disjoint inversions contribute; all factorial moments match Poisson(cΛ). First and second moments establish the other regimes. Gaussian overlap integration yields c(1+exp(-a²))/(4π). The finite checker using the actual verify.py passed 457 assertions; simulation is not mistaken for proof.

originality.rationale: The assessed source-specific result combines exact *simultaneous* constant-score equivalence for Meyer’s two summaries, a full three-regime N²σ threshold, a Poisson limiting law under fixed nonidentically distributed group laws, and a quantitative fixed-alternative power obstruction. Meyer defines the scores but does not give these results. Jeong–Dytso–Cardone develop noisy-permutation recovery and fixed-n small-noise errors but not this joint asymptotic theorem. General close-pair Poisson methods supply substantial non-new machinery; independent priority review is still necessary.
residual_risks: Silverman–Brown full text was unavailable, so only its general subject and published abstract were verified; it may yield the Poisson inversion count through known methods.
The rank-complementarity identity is elementary once the two score definitions are known; novelty is the combined quantitative statistical phase transition, not this isolated identity.
Further historical studies of marked close-pair Poisson limits or noisy sorting may contain analogous crossover formulas not surfaced in accessible full texts.
No independent expert audit or independent experimental certification has been performed.

value.rationale: The statistic transforms entire functional curves to single scalar ranks, so complete loss of group information on anti-phase curves is a direct failure boundary. The result gives an exact if-and-only-if loss event, a sharp N^-2 measurement-noise threshold, an explicit nonzero Poisson all-tie probability and a concrete 0.6322 power ceiling for separated smooth Gaussian groups. This quantitative boundary is useful for time-weighting and tie-handling decisions; no broader method performance claim is made.
